title: Is it proportional? Find the constant

slides.title: Three walkers, three tables
slides.text: Three walkers hand Tally their notes from the road into the village. Each one wrote the hours walked and the kilometers covered. Tally wants to know which walker kept one steady pace from the very start.

slides.title: The same number for 1 hour
slides.text: Two quantities are proportional when one is always the same number times the other. Divide each distance by its time. If every answer is the same, that number is the constant of proportionality, k. Here k = 3.

visual.label: A walker's table with the kilometers for each hour
head: Hours

focus.cue: In 1 hour the walker covers 3 kilometers.
Every column gives 3: that is k.

slides.title: A head start is not proportional
slides.text: This walker adds 2 kilometers each hour, so the table looks steady. But the walk began 1 kilometer down the road. Divide to check: the answers differ, so the distance is not proportional to the time.
steps: 1 h → 3 km, 2 h → 5 km, 3 h → 7 km

slides.title: On a graph: straight, through zero
slides.text: The graph of a proportional relationship is a straight line through the origin, the point (0, 0). The point (1, 3) shows the unit rate: 3 kilometers in 1 hour. As an equation, d = 3t.

visual.label: Distance against time for a steady walk

focus.cue: The line starts at the origin: 0 hours, 0 kilometers.
At 1 hour it is at 3: the unit rate.
One straight line, so the pace never changes.

slides.title: A unit rate from fractions
slides.text: A scout walks 1/2 kilometer in 1/4 hour. One hour is 4 quarter hours, so in one hour the scout walks 4 times as far: 2 kilometers. Dividing gives the same answer: 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 2 kilometers per hour.

words.means: one amount is always the same number times the other
that same number, k: the amount of one for each 1 of the other
how much for 1: kilometers in 1 hour, meters for 1 centimeter
the point (0, 0), where the two axes of a graph cross

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Scale Scout at Steady Pace. Check three walkers' tables, find the kilometers for 1 hour, and pick the graph that is proportional. A wrong plan shows you what it really gives.
slides.alt: Scale Scout on a phone: a paper map board with three small tables of hours and kilometers, lettered A, B and C, and three tiles to pick from.
